# 0. Overview

**Goal.** Targeted Random Projection (TARP; Mukhopadhyay and Dunson) predicts a response from millions of
predictors by (i) screening predictors with a randomized, correlation-based rule, (ii) compressing the survivors
with a sparse random projection, and (iii) fitting a closed-form Normal-Inverse-Gamma (NIG) Bayesian regression
on the compressed features, averaging over many projections. This document applies the method to a real
ultra-high-dimensional problem, tests it against strong alternatives, and checks the quality of its predictions
and prediction intervals.

**Scope (project description).** The study explores variable selection and screening methods, with a focus on **randomized Sure Independence Screening (SIS) projections**, and compares their performance with other approaches. It examines dimensionality reduction (random projection, PCA, randomized SVD), prediction, and the effects of correlation (linkage disequilibrium) and genetic structure (ancestry, relatedness) among the covariates, to understand how incorporating the underlying structure of high-dimensional genetic data can improve statistical modelling and variable selection. *Terminology:* SIS (Fan and Lv, 2008) keeps the top-d predictors by absolute marginal correlation; TARP's first step is its randomized version, randomized independence screening (RIS); a "random SIS projection" is RIS followed by a sparse random projection (RIS-RP).

**Data.** 1001 Genomes *Arabidopsis thaliana*: n = 1,003 accessions, p = 1,712,884 quality-filtered SNPs;
response = days to flowering at 10 °C (FT10, AraPheno study 12). A second flowering trait (FT16, same accessions
at 16 °C) is used for replication.

**Questions.**

1. Do the published TARP claims (aggregation needed; aggregated TARP comparable to PCA projection) hold on new data?
2. How do SIS, randomized SIS (RIS), iterated SIS and structure-adjusted SIS compare, and what do they select when the
   predictors are correlated (LD) and structured (ancestry)? Do they recover a planted truth?
3. Which implementation pitfalls change the conclusions of a screen-then-fit pipeline?
4. How does TARP compare with the standard dense baseline, GBLUP (kernel ridge on all SNPs)?
5. Does adding TARP-style screening on top of a dense kernel, or screening groups of correlated SNPs, help?
6. What is being predicted: population structure, relatedness, or within-lineage genetic signal?
7. Are the prediction intervals calibrated, including within ancestry groups?
8. Does the picture hold for a second trait?

**Evaluation protocol (used throughout).** Ten random 80/20 train/test splits of the 1,003 accessions, identical
across all experiments. Screening and all tuning use training rows only; the test set is touched once. Accuracy is
test mean squared prediction error (MSPE) and R-squared `1 - MSPE/MSPE(mean-only)` per split. Comparisons are paired
by split. The ten splits reuse the same accessions, so standard errors describe split-to-split variation only and
are optimistic.

**How this file runs.** It is self-contained. Heavy computations are cached in `cache/`; if the original checkpoint
files from earlier development runs are present in the project folder they are reused, so a first render takes
minutes. With no caches the full pipeline recomputes (several hours; progress is checkpointed per seed and
resumable). Set `USE_CACHE <- FALSE` to force recomputation.

```{r params}
N_CORES <- 3            # worker cores for bigstatsr; BLAS is pinned to one thread (see helpers)
N_REPS  <- 10           # random train/test splits per experiment
K_IN    <- 5            # inner folds for nested ("honest") tuning
USE_CACHE <- TRUE       # reuse cached results (cache/ or the original checkpoints) when present
RUN_SCALING <- FALSE    # re-run the scaling benchmark (about 10 minutes); otherwise recorded values are shown
K_DIM   <- 100          # dimension of the compressed space
LAM_GRID <- 10^seq(-3, 3, length.out = 61)
C_GRID  <- c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 16)                 # RBF bandwidth multipliers
W_GRID  <- c(0, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3)   # weight on the screened kernel
ALPHA <- 0.10; K_GROUPS <- 3; MIN_G <- 15            # conformal intervals
# optional third trait (e.g. a DOG1-related germination trait): fill in and re-render
THIRD_TRAIT <- list(file = NULL, id_col = "accession_id", y_col = NULL, name = "third trait")
```

# 1. Data and cleaning

The raw data are the 1001 Genomes release v3.1 (1,135 accessions, 12,883,854 candidate variants, about 19 GB
compressed) and the AraPheno flowering-time phenotypes (study 12). Cleaning is done once, outside R, with PLINK 2;
the commands are recorded below (not evaluated when this file is rendered). The R code in this document starts from
the PLINK output.

```bash
# 1. raw genotypes (about 19 GB)
wget -c https://1001genomes.org/data/GMI-MPI/releases/v3.1/1001genomes_snp-short-indel_only_ACGTN.vcf.gz

# 2. quality control and conversion to PLINK binary:
#    biallelic sites only, at most 10% missing calls, minor allele frequency >= 1%
plink2 --vcf 1001genomes_snp-short-indel_only_ACGTN.vcf.gz --allow-extra-chr --set-missing-var-ids @:# \
       --maf 0.01 --geno 0.1 --max-alleles 2 --threads 8 --make-bed --out arabidopsis_1135

# 3. phenotypes (FT10 and FT16 in one file)
wget https://arapheno.1001genomes.org/rest/study/12/values.csv -O flowering_time.csv

# 4. keep accessions that have BOTH genotype and phenotype
awk '{print $2}' arabidopsis_1135.fam | sort -u > geno_ids.txt
tail -n +2 flowering_time.csv | cut -d',' -f1 | sort -u > pheno_ids.txt
comm -12 geno_ids.txt pheno_ids.txt > matched_ids.txt
awk 'NR==FNR{a[$1];next} $2 in a {print $1, $2}' matched_ids.txt arabidopsis_1135.fam > keep_samples.txt
plink2 --bfile arabidopsis_1135 --keep keep_samples.txt --make-bed --out arabidopsis_1135_matched
```

```{r cleaning-table}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Step = c("Raw VCF", "Biallelic sites only (--max-alleles 2)", "Missingness filter (--geno 0.1)",
           "Rare-variant filter (--maf 0.01)", "Accessions with genotype and FT10 phenotype"),
  Remaining = c("12,883,854 variants x 1,135 accessions", "11,769,920 variants", "6,414,265 variants (5,654,946 removed)",
                "1,712,884 variants (4,402,090 removed)", "1,003 accessions (of 1,135 genotyped, 1,163 phenotyped)")),
  caption = "Data cleaning, as logged by PLINK 2")
```

Two facts about the genotype matrix matter later. This species self-pollinates, so there are **no heterozygous calls**
(every genotype is 0 or 2). About 5% of calls are missing (allowed by the 10% per-SNP threshold) and are mean-imputed
for modeling.

# 2. Setup and helper functions

```{r packages}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({ library(bigsnpr); library(bigstatsr); library(parallel) })
if (!requireNamespace("RhpcBLASctl", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Run once in a terminal: micromamba install -c conda-forge r-rhpcblasctl")
}
# bigstatsr refuses nested parallelism, so BLAS is pinned to one thread and parallelism comes from ncores
RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(1)
dir.create("cache", showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r helpers}
## ---------- generic infrastructure ----------
# Run fun(seed) for every seed, checkpointing each seed (resumable); reuse a final cache or a legacy checkpoint.
run_seeds <- function(name, fun, seeds = seq_len(N_REPS), legacy = NULL) {
  final <- file.path("cache", paste0(name, ".rds"))
  if (USE_CACHE && file.exists(final)) return(readRDS(final))
  if (USE_CACHE && !is.null(legacy) && file.exists(legacy)) {
    x <- readRDS(legacy); return(if (is.data.frame(x)) x else do.call(rbind, x))
  }
  part <- file.path("cache", paste0(name, "_partial.rds"))
  res <- if (file.exists(part)) readRDS(part) else list()
  for (s in seeds) {
    if (length(res) >= s && !is.null(res[[s]])) next
    t0 <- Sys.time(); res[[s]] <- fun(s); saveRDS(res, part)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] seed %d done in %.1f min\n", name, s, as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, res); saveRDS(out, final); out
}
make_split <- function(seed_i, pool = seq_len(n)) {      # same RNG path as every experiment
  set.seed(seed_i)
  tr <- sample(pool, size = round(0.8 * length(pool)))
  list(tr = tr, te = setdiff(pool, tr))
}
sem <- function(x) sd(x) / sqrt(length(x))

## ---------- TARP building blocks ----------
# Step 1: randomized independence screening using ONLY the given training rows.
screen_set <- function(tr_rows, y_vec) {
  gw <- big_univLinReg(G2, y.train = y_vec, ind.train = tr_rows, ncores = N_CORES)
  tt <- gw$estim / gw$std.err
  r <- sign(tt) * sqrt(tt^2 / (tt^2 + (length(tr_rows) - 2))); r[is.na(r)] <- 0   # marginal correlation
  delta <- max(0, (1 + log(p / length(tr_rows))) / 2)
  q_in <- abs(r)^delta; q_in <- q_in / max(q_in)                                  # inclusion probabilities
  list(inc = which(rbinom(p, 1, q_in) == 1), r = r)
}
std_cols <- function(Xs, tr_rows, other_rows) {          # standardize with training statistics only
  cm <- colMeans(Xs[tr_rows, ]); cs <- apply(Xs[tr_rows, ], 2, sd); cs[cs == 0] <- 1
  list(tr = scale(Xs[tr_rows, ], center = cm, scale = cs), other = scale(Xs[other_rows, ], center = cm, scale = cs))
}
screened_gram <- function(inc) {                          # n x n kernel of the screened SNPs over all rows
  Xs <- G2[, inc]; cs <- apply(Xs, 2, sd); keep <- cs > 0
  Xs <- scale(Xs[, keep, drop = FALSE], center = TRUE, scale = cs[keep])
  tcrossprod(Xs) / sum(keep)
}
# Step 2: sparse ternary random matrix, entries +-1/sqrt(2 psi) with probability psi each
tarp_omega <- function(p_gamma, l, psi = 0.25) {
  u <- runif(p_gamma * l); Om <- matrix(0, p_gamma, l); val <- 1 / sqrt(2 * psi)
  Om[u < psi] <- val; Om[u >= psi & u < 2 * psi] <- -val; Om
}
# Step 3: closed-form NIG fit on the compressed features; returns test MSPE
nig_mspe <- function(Z_tr, Z_te, y_c, y_mean, y_te) {
  m <- ncol(Z_tr); mu <- solve(diag(m) + crossprod(Z_tr), crossprod(Z_tr, y_c))
  mean((y_te - ((Z_te %*% mu) + y_mean))^2)
}
# Paper's aggregation: B projections with m_n ~ U[2 log p, 3n/4], simple average of predictions
agg_tarp_pred <- function(X_tr, X_te, y_c, y_mean, p_total, B = 100) {
  p_g <- ncol(X_tr); n_tr <- nrow(X_tr); m_rng <- c(2 * log(p_total), 3 * n_tr / 4)
  rowMeans(vapply(seq_len(B), function(b) {
    m_b <- round(runif(1, m_rng[1], m_rng[2])); Om <- tarp_omega(p_g, m_b)
    Z_tr <- X_tr %*% Om; Z_te <- X_te %*% Om
    mu <- solve(diag(m_b) + crossprod(Z_tr), crossprod(Z_tr, y_c))
    as.numeric((Z_te %*% mu) + y_mean)
  }, numeric(nrow(X_te))))
}
# Randomized SVD (Halko-Martinsson-Tropp) with TARP's sparse matrix as the sketch and q power iterations
rsvd_basis <- function(X, k, q, l = k + 10, psi = 0.25) {
  Q <- qr.Q(qr(X %*% tarp_omega(ncol(X), l, psi)))
  for (i in seq_len(q)) { W <- qr.Q(qr(crossprod(X, Q))); Q <- qr.Q(qr(X %*% W)) }
  B <- crossprod(Q, X); e <- eigen(tcrossprod(B), symmetric = TRUE)
  sweep(crossprod(B, e$vectors[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]), 2, sqrt(pmax(e$values[1:k], 1e-12)), "/")
}
gram_pca_basis <- function(X, k) {                        # exact PCA directions via the n x n Gram matrix
  e <- eigen(tcrossprod(X), symmetric = TRUE)
  sweep(crossprod(X, e$vectors[, 1:k, drop = FALSE]), 2, sqrt(e$values[1:k]), "/")
}
energy <- function(X, V) sum((X %*% V)^2)

## ---------- kernel ridge / GBLUP building blocks ----------
log_evidence <- function(e_scaled, ytil2, rest_ss, n_, a = 0.01, b = 0.01) {   # closed-form NIG marginal likelihood
  s <- 1 + e_scaled; q <- sum(ytil2 / s) + rest_ss
  -0.5 * sum(log(s)) + a * log(b) - lgamma(a) + lgamma(a + n_ / 2) - (a + n_ / 2) * log(b + 0.5 * q)
}
# one eigendecomposition gives LOOCV, evidence and test error for every lambda
kernel_all <- function(K, K_new, y_c, y_new_c, lam_grid) {
  n_ <- length(y_c)
  eg <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); e <- pmax(eg$values, 0); U <- eg$vectors
  yt <- as.numeric(crossprod(U, y_c))
  S <- outer(e, lam_grid, function(ei, li) ei / (ei + li))
  h <- (U^2) %*% S; yhat <- U %*% (S * yt)
  loo <- colMeans(((y_c - yhat) / pmax(1 - h, 1e-8))^2)
  ev <- vapply(lam_grid, function(l) log_evidence(e / l, yt^2, 0, n_), numeric(1))
  P <- K_new %*% (U %*% (yt / outer(e, lam_grid, "+")))
  list(loo = loo, ev = ev, test = colMeans((y_new_c - P)^2), pred = P)
}
kernel_curve <- function(K, K_new, y_c, lam_grid) {       # predictions of the centered response for every lambda
  eg <- eigen(K, symmetric = TRUE); e <- pmax(eg$values, 0); U <- eg$vectors
  yt <- as.numeric(crossprod(U, y_c))
  K_new %*% (U %*% (yt / outer(e, lam_grid, "+")))
}
mse_curve <- function(pred_c, y_new_c) colMeans((y_new_c - pred_c)^2)
gblup_fit <- function(tr, te, y_tr, lam_grid = LAM_GRID) {  # GBLUP with LOOCV lambda (valid: no supervised screening)
  ym <- mean(y_tr); kk <- kernel_all(Kfull[tr, tr], Kfull[te, tr], y_tr - ym, rep(0, length(te)), lam_grid)
  il <- which.min(kk$loo); list(pred = kk$pred[, il] + ym, lam = lam_grid[il])
}
gdist <- function(rows, cols) outer(dK[rows], dK[cols], "+") - 2 * Kfull[rows, cols]   # squared genomic distance
```


# 3. Data description

```{r load-data}
if (!file.exists("arabidopsis_1135_matched.rds")) snp_readBed("arabidopsis_1135_matched.bed")
obj.bigSNP <- snp_attach("arabidopsis_1135_matched.rds")
G <- obj.bigSNP$genotypes; map <- obj.bigSNP$map; fam <- obj.bigSNP$fam
if (!file.exists("flowering_time.csv")) {
  download.file("https://arapheno.1001genomes.org/rest/study/12/values.csv", "flowering_time.csv", mode = "wb")
}
pheno <- read.csv("flowering_time.csv")
y_all <- pheno$FT10[match(as.character(fam$sample.ID), as.character(pheno$accession_id))]   # main response
y16   <- pheno$FT16[match(as.character(fam$sample.ID), as.character(pheno$accession_id))]   # second trait
n <- nrow(G); p <- ncol(G)
stopifnot(sum(is.na(y_all)) == 0)
G2 <- snp_fastImputeSimple(G, method = "mean2", ncores = N_CORES)   # mean-imputed copy used for modeling
cat("accessions n =", n, "| SNPs p =", format(p, big.mark = ","), "| p/n =", round(p / n), "\n")
```

```{r genotype-summary, fig.height = 4.5}

tot <- rowSums(cnt)
geno_tab <- data.frame(State = c("0 (reference allele)", "1 (heterozygous)", "2 (alternate allele)", "missing"),
                       Calls = tot, Share = tot / sum(tot))
knitr::kable(geno_tab, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE, format.args = list(big.mark = ","),
             caption = "Genotype calls over all accessions and SNPs (zero heterozygotes: the species self-pollinates)")
f_alt <- cnt[3, ] / pmax(cnt[1, ] + cnt[3, ], 1); maf <- pmin(f_alt, 1 - f_alt); miss <- cnt[4, ] / n
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
barplot(tot / sum(tot), names.arg = c("0", "1 (het)", "2", "NA"), col = "steelblue", border = NA,
        ylab = "share of calls", main = "Genotype states")
hist(maf, breaks = 40, col = "steelblue", border = "white", xlab = "minor allele frequency", main = "MAF of the 1.7M SNPs")
hist(miss, breaks = 40, col = "steelblue", border = "white", xlab = "fraction of accessions missing", main = "Per-SNP missingness")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r phenotype-plots, fig.height = 4.5}
ok16 <- !is.na(y16)
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
hist(y_all, breaks = 30, col = "steelblue", border = "white", xlab = "days", main = "FT10: days to flowering at 10 C")
hist(y16[ok16], breaks = 30, col = "darkorange", border = "white", xlab = "days", main = "FT16: days to flowering at 16 C")
plot(y_all[ok16], y16[ok16], pch = 16, cex = 0.5, col = rgb(0, 0, 0, 0.35), xlab = "FT10", ylab = "FT16",
     main = sprintf("FT10 vs FT16 (r = %.2f)", cor(y_all[ok16], y16[ok16])))
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
cat(sprintf("FT10: mean %.1f, sd %.1f, range %.0f-%.0f days (n = %d).  FT16 available for %d of these accessions.\n",
            mean(y_all), sd(y_all), min(y_all), max(y_all), n, sum(ok16)))
```

FT16 is the same panel measured at a second temperature, so it is strongly correlated with FT10: it is a replication
on a **related** trait, not a trait with an independent genetic architecture.

## 3.1 Genome-wide relationship matrix and population structure

GBLUP, the dense baseline used below, needs the n x n genomic relationship matrix over **all** SNPs. It is built in
one blockwise pass (20,000 SNPs per block; each block standardized with all accessions, no response involved) and
cached; this one-time pass takes on the order of 20 minutes and is reused for every trait and split.

```{r gram}
gram_file <- "gram_full_snp.rds"
if (!file.exists(gram_file)) {
  RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(N_CORES)                 # no bigstatsr parallel call inside this loop
  Kfull <- matrix(0, n, n); p_used <- 0
  blocks <- split(seq_len(p), ceiling(seq_len(p) / 20000)); t0 <- Sys.time()
  for (b in seq_along(blocks)) {
    Xb <- G2[, blocks[[b]]]; cm <- colMeans(Xb); cs <- apply(Xb, 2, sd); keep <- cs > 0
    Xb <- scale(Xb[, keep, drop = FALSE], center = cm[keep], scale = cs[keep])
    Kfull <- Kfull + tcrossprod(Xb); p_used <- p_used + sum(keep); rm(Xb)
    if (b %% 10 == 0) cat(sprintf("Gram block %d / %d (%.1f min)\n", b, length(blocks), as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "mins"))))
  }
  RhpcBLASctl::blas_set_num_threads(1)
  saveRDS(list(K = Kfull / p_used, p_used = p_used), gram_file); rm(Kfull)
}
gr <- readRDS(gram_file); Kfull <- gr$K; dK <- diag(Kfull)
cat("Gram matrix", dim(Kfull), "built from", format(gr$p_used, big.mark = ","), "non-constant SNPs; mean diagonal", round(mean(dK), 3), "\n")
```

```{r structure-plot, fig.height = 5}
eK <- eigen(Kfull, symmetric = TRUE)
pcs5 <- sweep(eK$vectors[, 1:5], 2, sqrt(eK$values[1:5]), "*")        # top genomic axes (ancestry gradients)
var_share <- eK$values / sum(eK$values)
col_ft <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "yellow", "red"))(100)[cut(y_all, 100, labels = FALSE)]
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
barplot(100 * var_share[1:15], names.arg = 1:15, col = "steelblue", border = NA, xlab = "genomic axis",
        ylab = "% of genome-wide variance", main = "Population structure: kernel eigenvalues")
plot(pcs5[, 1], pcs5[, 2], pch = 16, cex = 0.6, col = col_ft, xlab = "axis 1", ylab = "axis 2",
     main = "Accessions on the first two axes\n(blue = early flowering, red = late)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
cat(sprintf("The first axis alone carries %.1f%% of genome-wide variance; the first five carry %.1f%%.\n",
            100 * var_share[1], 100 * sum(var_share[1:5])))
```

One axis dominates the genome-wide variation and the phenotype varies along it: ancestry and flowering time are
entangled. That is why population structure, relatedness and within-lineage signal are separated explicitly in
Section 7.

```{r groups}
# three ancestry clusters from the first five axes (unsupervised, no response); used for Mondrian conformal intervals
set.seed(2024)
grp <- kmeans(pcs5, centers = K_GROUPS, nstart = 25)$cluster
cat("ancestry cluster sizes:", paste(table(grp), collapse = " / "), "| mean FT10 by cluster:",
    paste(round(tapply(y_all, grp, mean), 1), collapse = " / "), "\n")
```

# 4. Replicating TARP: aggregation, PCA projection and randomized SVD

**Method (TARP, per the paper).** For each SNP compute its marginal correlation $r_j$ with the response; keep it with
probability $q_j \propto |r_j|^{\delta}$, $\delta = \max\{0,(1+\log(p/n))/2\}$; compress the $p_\gamma$ survivors with a
sparse random matrix $R$ (entries $\pm 1/\sqrt{2\psi}$ w.p. $\psi$, else 0) to $Z = XR'$ and fit the conjugate model
$y = Z\theta + \varepsilon$ with prior $\theta\mid\sigma^2 \sim N(0,\sigma^2 I)$, giving
$\mu_t = (I + Z'Z)^{-1}Z'y$ and a Student-t predictive distribution. A **single** projection is noisy, so the paper
averages predictions over 100 projections with $m_n \sim U[2\log p,\,3n/4]$.

**Variants compared on the same screened SNPs.** (i) one projection, (ii) the 100-draw aggregation, (iii) exact PCA
projection (RIS-PCR), and (iv) a randomized-SVD projection that uses TARP's own sparse matrix as the sketch followed by
`q` power iterations: `q = 0` is a data-adaptive rotation of one sketch, and `q -> infinity` recovers PCA, so `q` is a
single knob between random projection and PCA.

```{r si-run}
QS <- c(0, 1, 2, 4)
run_rep_si <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - y_mean
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr)                                  # RNG continues straight from the split
  X <- std_cols(G2[, sc$inc], tr, te); X_tr <- X$tr; X_te <- X$other; p_g <- ncol(X_tr)
  out <- list(seed = seed_i, baseline = mean((y_te - y_mean)^2), n_screened = p_g)
  tm <- system.time({ pca <- prcomp(X_tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM) })[["elapsed"]]
  V_pca <- pca$rotation[, 1:K_DIM]
  out$PCA <- nig_mspe(X_tr %*% V_pca, X_te %*% V_pca, y_c, y_mean, y_te); out$t_PCA <- tm
  E_pca <- energy(X_tr, V_pca)
  Om <- tarp_omega(p_g, K_DIM); out$RP_single <- nig_mspe(X_tr %*% Om, X_te %*% Om, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
  tm <- system.time({ pa <- agg_tarp_pred(X_tr, X_te, y_c, y_mean, p, B = 100) })[["elapsed"]]
  out$RP_agg <- mean((y_te - pa)^2); out$t_RP_agg <- tm
  for (qq in QS) {
    tm <- system.time({ V <- rsvd_basis(X_tr, K_DIM, qq) })[["elapsed"]]
    out[[paste0("SI_q", qq)]] <- nig_mspe(X_tr %*% V, X_te %*% V, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
    out[[paste0("E_q", qq)]] <- energy(X_tr, V) / E_pca; out[[paste0("t_q", qq)]] <- tm
  }
  as.data.frame(out)
}
si <- run_seeds("si", run_rep_si, legacy = "si_replication_results.rds")
base_s <- setNames(si$baseline, si$seed)             # per-split mean-only MSPE, shared by every experiment
r2_of <- function(v, seeds = names(v)) 1 - v / base_s[seeds]
cat("splits:", nrow(si), "| SNPs surviving screening per split (mean):", round(mean(si$n_screened)), "\n")
```

```{r si-plots, fig.height = 5.5}

**Scaling benchmark.** Wall time for exact SVD (`prcomp`), exact PCA through the n x n Gram matrix, randomized SVD
(q = 2) and the paper's 100-draw aggregation (extrapolated from 5 draws) as the number of screened SNPs grows. Unless
`RUN_SCALING <- TRUE`, the values recorded in the original run (single-threaded, same laptop) are shown.

```{r scaling}
scaling <- data.frame(p_screened = c(5000, 20000, 50000, 100000),
  exact_svd = c(8.953, 35.725, 91.573, 189.92), exact_gram = c(2.822, 11.013, 23.434, 47.048),
  rsvd_q2 = c(2.23, 9.163, 24.314, 47.25), tarp_agg100_extrap = c(86.96, 366.92, 908.38, 1796.46),
  rsvd_energy_vs_exact = c(0.9975744, 0.9951787, 0.9925784, 0.9891172))
if (RUN_SCALING) {
  sp1 <- make_split(1); gw <- big_univLinReg(G2, y.train = y_all[sp1$tr], ind.train = sp1$tr, ncores = N_CORES)
  ord <- order(abs(gw$estim / gw$std.err), decreasing = TRUE); ord[is.na(ord)] <- length(ord)
  scaling <- do.call(rbind, lapply(scaling$p_screened, function(K) {
    X <- G2[sp1$tr, ord[1:K]]; cs <- apply(X, 2, sd); cs[cs == 0] <- 1; X <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = cs)
    t_svd <- system.time(prcomp(X, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM))[["elapsed"]]
    t_gram <- system.time(Vg <- gram_pca_basis(X, K_DIM))[["elapsed"]]
    t_rsvd <- system.time(Vr <- rsvd_basis(X, K_DIM, 2))[["elapsed"]]
    t_agg5 <- system.time(for (b in 1:5) { Zb <- X %*% tarp_omega(K, 315) })[["elapsed"]]
    data.frame(p_screened = K, exact_svd = t_svd, exact_gram = t_gram, rsvd_q2 = t_rsvd,
               tarp_agg100_extrap = t_agg5 * 20, rsvd_energy_vs_exact = energy(X, Vr) / energy(X, Vg))
  }))
}
knitr::kable(scaling, digits = 3, caption = "Seconds to obtain 100 projection directions (and rSVD energy relative to exact)")
matplot(scaling$p_screened, scaling[, c("exact_svd", "exact_gram", "rsvd_q2", "tarp_agg100_extrap")], type = "b", pch = 1:4,
        lty = 1, log = "xy", col = c("grey40", "blue", "steelblue", "darkgreen"), xlab = "screened SNPs (log scale)",
        ylab = "seconds (log scale)", main = "Cost of compressing the screened SNPs")
legend("topleft", c("exact SVD", "exact PCA via Gram matrix", "randomized SVD (q = 2)", "TARP, 100 draws (extrapolated)"),
       col = c("grey40", "blue", "steelblue", "darkgreen"), pch = 1:4, lty = 1, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
```

            mean(si$RP_single), mean(si$RP_agg), mean(si$PCA), mean(si$baseline)))

            mean(d_agg), sem(d_agg), sum(d_agg < 0), nrow(si)))

            mean(si$SI_q0 - si$PCA), mean(si$SI_q2 - si$PCA), 100 * mean(si$E_q2)))

            scaling$rsvd_q2[4], scaling$tarp_agg100_extrap[4], scaling$tarp_agg100_extrap[4] / scaling$rsvd_q2[4],
            scaling$exact_svd[4], scaling$exact_gram[4]))

# 5. Screening and variable selection: SIS, randomized SIS, iterated SIS and structure-adjusted SIS

**Terminology.** *Sure Independence Screening* (SIS; Fan and Lv, 2008) ranks predictors by the absolute marginal
correlation $|r_j|$ with the response and keeps the top $d$ (default $d=\lfloor n/\log n\rfloor$, here 120 for
n = 802 training accessions). TARP's first step is the *randomized* version, **randomized independence screening
(RIS)**: SNP $j$ survives with probability $q_j\propto|r_j|^{\delta}$, a soft threshold with no hard cutoff.
**"Random SIS projection" = RIS followed by a sparse random projection (RIS-RP)**, the method evaluated in
Section 4. This section studies the screening step itself, how it behaves when predictors are strongly correlated
(linkage disequilibrium, LD) and structured (ancestry), and how it compares with the alternatives:

| Screen | Rule |
|---|---|
| `SIS` (d = n/log n, 2000, or the RIS survivor count) | deterministic top-$d$ by absolute marginal correlation |
| `RIS` | Bernoulli($q_j$) with $q_j$ proportional to (absolute marginal correlation)$^{\delta}$ (TARP step 1) |
| `ISIS` | iterated SIS: select, fit a lasso, take residuals, re-screen (3 rounds) |
| `SISadj` | SIS on the response after removing the first five genomic (ancestry) axes |

After screening, the survivors are modeled with the lasso, ridge or elastic net (`glmnet`), the standard
"SIS + penalized regression" recipe, and compared with TARP's projections and with the dense GBLUP baseline.

```{r sis-helpers}
HAS_GLMNET <- requireNamespace("glmnet", quietly = TRUE)
if (!HAS_GLMNET) message("glmnet is not installed: lasso/ridge-after-screening rows are skipped. ",
                         "Install once with: micromamba install -c conda-forge r-glmnet")
screen_scores <- function(tr_rows, y_vec) {              # signed t-statistic of every SNP against y_vec (training rows only)
  gw <- big_univLinReg(G2, y.train = y_vec, ind.train = tr_rows, ncores = N_CORES)
  tt <- gw$estim / gw$std.err; tt[is.na(tt)] <- 0; tt
}
sis_top <- function(score, d) order(abs(score), decreasing = TRUE)[1:d]
adjust_response <- function(tr_rows, y_vec) resid(lm(y_vec ~ pcs5[tr_rows, , drop = FALSE]))   # remove ancestry axes
isis_set <- function(tr_rows, y_vec, d_total, n_iter = 3) {
  d_step <- ceiling(d_total / n_iter); sel <- integer(0); y_c <- y_vec - mean(y_vec); y_res <- y_c
  for (it in seq_len(n_iter)) {
    tt <- screen_scores(tr_rows, y_res); tt[sel] <- 0
    sel <- c(sel, order(abs(tt), decreasing = TRUE)[1:d_step])
    if (it < n_iter) {
      Xs <- scale(G2[tr_rows, sel, drop = FALSE]); Xs[is.na(Xs)] <- 0
      fit <- if (HAS_GLMNET) {
        cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(Xs, y_c, alpha = 1, nfolds = 5); as.numeric(predict(cv, Xs, s = "lambda.min"))
      } else {
        as.numeric(Xs %*% solve(crossprod(Xs) + 0.1 * length(tr_rows) * diag(ncol(Xs)), crossprod(Xs, y_c)))
      }
      y_res <- y_c - fit
    }
  }
  sel
}
# penalized fit on a screened set; lambda by glmnet's internal 10-fold CV (in-sample, so subject to the screening
# bias discussed in Section 6, but the test MSPE below is untouched by it); optionally ancestry axes unpenalized
pen_fit <- function(sel, tr, te, y_tr, y_te, alpha, pcs_cov = FALSE) {
  if (!HAS_GLMNET) return(c(mspe = NA_real_, nz = NA_real_))
  X <- std_cols(G2[, sel, drop = FALSE], tr, te); keep <- apply(X$tr, 2, sd) > 1e-8
  x_tr <- X$tr[, keep, drop = FALSE]; x_te <- X$other[, keep, drop = FALSE]; pf <- rep(1, ncol(x_tr))
  if (pcs_cov) { x_tr <- cbind(pcs5[tr, ], x_tr); x_te <- cbind(pcs5[te, ], x_te); pf <- c(rep(0, ncol(pcs5)), pf) }
  cv <- glmnet::cv.glmnet(x_tr, y_tr, alpha = alpha, nfolds = 10, penalty.factor = pf)
  pr <- as.numeric(predict(cv, x_te, s = "lambda.min"))
  c(mspe = mean((y_te - pr)^2), nz = sum(as.numeric(coef(cv, s = "lambda.min"))[-1] != 0))
}
```

## 5.1 Prediction after screening: SIS, RIS, ISIS and structure-adjusted SIS with penalized regression

```{r sis-run}
run_rep_sis <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; ym <- mean(y_tr)
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr)                                 # RIS survivors
  tt <- screen_scores(tr, y_tr)
  d1 <- floor(length(tr) / log(length(tr))); d2 <- 2000; dR <- length(sc$inc)
  S <- list(SIS1 = sis_top(tt, d1), SIS2 = sis_top(tt, d2), SISR = sis_top(tt, dR), RIS = sc$inc,
            ADJ2 = sis_top(screen_scores(tr, adjust_response(tr, y_tr)), d2), ISIS2 = isis_set(tr, y_tr, d2))
  f <- function(sel, alpha, pc = FALSE) pen_fit(sel, tr, te, y_tr, y_te, alpha, pc)
  r1 <- f(S$SIS1, 1); r2 <- f(S$SIS2, 1); r3 <- f(S$SIS2, 0); r4 <- f(S$SISR, 0); r5 <- f(S$RIS, 0)
  r6 <- f(S$ISIS2, 1); r7 <- f(S$ADJ2, 1, TRUE); r8 <- f(S$ADJ2, 0, TRUE)
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, baseline = mean((y_te - ym)^2), d1 = d1, dR = dR,
    SIS_d1_lasso = unname(r1["mspe"]), SIS_2000_lasso = unname(r2["mspe"]), SIS_2000_ridge = unname(r3["mspe"]),
    SIS_RISsize_ridge = unname(r4["mspe"]), RIS_ridge = unname(r5["mspe"]), ISIS_2000_lasso = unname(r6["mspe"]),
    SISadj_2000_lasso_pc = unname(r7["mspe"]), SISadj_2000_ridge_pc = unname(r8["mspe"]),
    nz_SIS_d1_lasso = unname(r1["nz"]), nz_SIS_2000_lasso = unname(r2["nz"]), nz_ISIS_2000_lasso = unname(r6["nz"]),
    nz_SISadj_2000_lasso_pc = unname(r7["nz"]),
    GBLUP = mean((y_te - gblup_fit(tr, te, y_tr)$pred)^2))
}
sis_res <- run_seeds("sis", run_rep_sis)
```

## 5.2 What the screens actually select: ancestry tagging, redundancy and LD blocks

Marginal screening ranks SNPs one at a time, so two things can go wrong in genetic data: (i) SNPs that merely **tag
ancestry** score highly because the phenotype tracks ancestry, and (ii) a single causal locus is represented by
**many near-duplicate SNPs** in LD, wasting the screening budget. Three diagnostics quantify this for each screen:
the mean absolute correlation of the selected SNPs with the first ancestry axis, the mean pairwise correlation among
selected SNPs, and the number of distinct loci (selected SNPs merged when within 50 kb).

```{r sel-diag}
sel_cache <- file.path("cache", "sel_sets.rds")
if (USE_CACHE && file.exists(sel_cache)) {
  sel_sets <- readRDS(sel_cache)
} else {
  sel_sets <- lapply(seq_len(N_REPS), function(s) {
    sp <- make_split(s); tr <- sp$tr; y_tr <- y_all[tr]
    sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); tt <- screen_scores(tr, y_tr)
    list(SIS_d1 = sis_top(tt, floor(length(tr) / log(length(tr)))), SIS_2000 = sis_top(tt, 2000), RIS = sc$inc,
         SISadj_2000 = sis_top(screen_scores(tr, adjust_response(tr, y_tr)), 2000))
  })
  saveRDS(sel_sets, sel_cache)
}
chr_int <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(map$chromosome)); pos_bp <- map$physical.pos
anc_axis <- as.numeric(scale(pcs5[, 1]))
sel_metrics <- function(sel) {
  Xs <- scale(G2[, sel, drop = FALSE]); Xs[is.na(Xs)] <- 0
  anc <- mean(abs(crossprod(anc_axis, Xs)) / (n - 1))
  sub <- Xs[, sample(ncol(Xs), min(ncol(Xs), 400)), drop = FALSE]
  cm <- abs(crossprod(sub)) / (n - 1); redund <- (sum(cm) - ncol(sub)) / (ncol(sub)^2 - ncol(sub))
  o <- order(chr_int[sel], pos_bp[sel]); ch <- chr_int[sel][o]; ps <- pos_bp[sel][o]
  loci <- 1 + sum(ch[-1] != ch[-length(ch)] | diff(ps) > 50000, na.rm = TRUE)
  c(anc_cor = anc, pairwise_cor = redund, loci = loci, size = length(sel))
}
set.seed(11)
diag_df <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(sel_sets), function(s) do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sel_sets[[s]]), function(m)
  data.frame(seed = s, set = m, t(sel_metrics(sel_sets[[s]][[m]])))))))
agg_diag <- aggregate(cbind(anc_cor, pairwise_cor, loci, size) ~ set, data = diag_df, FUN = mean)
knitr::kable(agg_diag, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Mean over splits")
rand_anc <- mean(abs(crossprod(anc_axis, {Z <- scale(G2[, sample(p, 2000)]); Z[is.na(Z)] <- 0; Z})) / (n - 1))
cat(sprintf("Reference: 2,000 random SNPs have mean |correlation| with ancestry axis 1 of %.3f.\n", rand_anc))
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
barplot(setNames(agg_diag$anc_cor, agg_diag$set), las = 2, col = "steelblue", border = NA, cex.names = 0.7,
        ylab = "mean |cor| with ancestry axis 1", main = "Ancestry tagging")
abline(h = rand_anc, lty = 2)
barplot(setNames(agg_diag$pairwise_cor, agg_diag$set), las = 2, col = "darkorange", border = NA, cex.names = 0.7,
        ylab = "mean pairwise |cor| among selected", main = "Redundancy (LD)")
barplot(setNames(agg_diag$loci / agg_diag$size, agg_diag$set), las = 2, col = "darkgreen", border = NA, cex.names = 0.7,
        ylab = "distinct loci per selected SNP", main = "Efficiency of the selected set")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

jacc <- function(a, b) length(intersect(a, b)) / length(union(a, b))
stab <- sapply(names(sel_sets[[1]]), function(m)
  mean(combn(length(sel_sets), 2, function(ij) jacc(sel_sets[[ij[1]]][[m]], sel_sets[[ij[2]]][[m]]))))
barplot(stab, col = "steelblue", border = NA, las = 2, cex.names = 0.8, ylab = "mean Jaccard overlap between splits",
        main = "Stability of the selected set across the 10 splits")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Screen = names(stab), Mean_Jaccard = round(stab, 3)), row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "1 = identical sets on every split; each pair of splits shares about 64% of its training accessions")
```

```{r ld-structure, fig.height = 5}
# LD decay: mean r^2 against physical distance, from windows on random chromosomes at three SNP strides
set.seed(77)
ld_pairs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(c(1, 10, 50), function(stride) do.call(rbind, lapply(1:15, function(i) {
  ch <- sample(1:5, 1); idx_ch <- which(chr_int == ch)
  st <- sample(seq_len(length(idx_ch) - 400 * stride), 1); idx <- idx_ch[st + stride * (0:399)]
  r2 <- suppressWarnings(cor(G2[, idx]))^2; dd <- abs(outer(pos_bp[idx], pos_bp[idx], "-"))
  ut <- upper.tri(r2); keep <- ut & !is.na(r2)
  data.frame(dist = dd[keep], r2 = r2[keep])
}))))
brk <- c(0, 500, 1e3, 2e3, 5e3, 1e4, 2e4, 5e4, 1e5, 2e5, 5e5)
ld_pairs$bin <- cut(ld_pairs$dist, brk, include.lowest = TRUE)
ld_curve <- aggregate(r2 ~ bin, data = ld_pairs, FUN = mean)
mids <- sqrt(brk[-length(brk)] * pmax(brk[-1], 1)); mids[1] <- 250; names(mids) <- levels(ld_pairs$bin)
ld_curve$mid <- mids[as.character(ld_curve$bin)]
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
plot(ld_curve$mid / 1000, ld_curve$r2, type = "b", pch = 19, log = "x", xlab = "distance between SNPs (kb, log scale)",
     ylab = "mean r^2", main = "Linkage disequilibrium decay")
sel_h <- sort(sel_sets[[1]]$SIS_2000[1:80]); o <- order(chr_int[sel_h], pos_bp[sel_h]); sel_h <- sel_h[o]
cm <- abs(suppressWarnings(cor(G2[, sel_h]))); cm[is.na(cm)] <- 0
image(1:80, 1:80, cm[, 80:1], col = hcl.colors(30, "YlOrRd", rev = TRUE), xlab = "top-80 SIS SNPs, in genome order", ylab = "",
      axes = FALSE, main = "|correlation| among the 80 top SIS SNPs")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

LD decays over tens of kilobases, so SNPs near a causal locus are nearly interchangeable for marginal screening; the
heatmap shows that the very top SIS picks fall into a few correlated blocks.

abline(v = c(fri, flc), col = "darkgreen", lty = 2); text(c(fri, flc), max(r1[ok]), c("FRI (approx.)", "FLC (approx.)"), pos = 4, col = "darkgreen", cex = 0.7)

knitr::kable(data.frame(chr = chr_int[top15], pos = pos_bp[top15], abs_t = round(r1[top15], 2),
   bp_to_FRI = ifelse(chr_int[top15] == 4, abs(pos_bp[top15] - 270000), NA),
   bp_to_FLC = ifelse(chr_int[top15] == 5, abs(pos_bp[top15] - 3176000), NA)), row.names = FALSE,
   caption = "Top 15 SNPs by |t| (training rows, split 1); distances use approximate gene positions")
```

## 5.3 Semi-synthetic simulation: does screening recover the truth, and what do LD and ancestry do to it?

On real data the causal SNPs are unknown. This simulation keeps the **real genotypes** (so the real LD and ancestry
structure are present) and plants a known signal:

$$y = \underbrace{\textstyle\sum_{j\in S}\beta_j \tilde x_j}_{\text{genetic, variance }h^2_g} + \underbrace{\gamma\,\tilde u_1}_{\text{ancestry, variance }h^2_a} + \varepsilon ,\qquad |S|=s,$$

with $\tilde x_j$ standardized causal SNPs and $\tilde u_1$ the first ancestry axis. Scenarios: **A** sparse (s = 20,
$h^2_g=0.5$, no ancestry effect); **B** sparse with ancestry confounding (s = 20, $h^2_g=0.3$, $h^2_a=0.4$);
**C** polygenic (s = 2000, $h^2_g=0.5$). Each screen is run on a training split and scored by
**exact recovery** (fraction of causal SNPs selected), **locus recovery** (fraction of causal SNPs having a selected SNP
with $|r|\ge 0.7$, i.e. tagged through LD) and **ancestry tagging** (mean $|r|$ of selected SNPs with axis 1).

```{r sim-run}
SIM_B <- 12
sim_scenarios <- list(A_sparse = list(s = 20, h2g = 0.5, h2a = 0), B_sparse_ancestry = list(s = 20, h2g = 0.3, h2a = 0.4),
                      C_polygenic = list(s = 2000, h2g = 0.5, h2a = 0))
sim_one <- function(scn_name, b) {
  scn <- sim_scenarios[[scn_name]]
  set.seed(5000 + b + 100 * match(scn_name, names(sim_scenarios)))
  causal <- sample(which(maf >= 0.1), scn$s)
  Xc <- scale(G2[, causal]); Xc[is.na(Xc)] <- 0
  g <- as.numeric(Xc %*% rnorm(scn$s)); g <- (g - mean(g)) / sd(g) * sqrt(scn$h2g)
  a <- anc_axis * sqrt(scn$h2a); e <- rnorm(n) * sqrt(max(1 - scn$h2g - scn$h2a, 0.01))
  y <- g + a + e
  sp <- make_split(9000 + b); tr <- sp$tr
  tt <- screen_scores(tr, y[tr]); r <- sign(tt) * sqrt(tt^2 / (tt^2 + length(tr) - 2))
  q_in <- abs(r)^max(0, (1 + log(p / length(tr))) / 2); q_in <- q_in / max(q_in)
  ris <- which(rbinom(p, 1, q_in) == 1)
  tt_adj <- screen_scores(tr, adjust_response(tr, y[tr]))
  d1 <- floor(length(tr) / log(length(tr)))
  sets <- list(SIS_d120 = sis_top(tt, d1), SIS_d2000 = sis_top(tt, 2000), RIS = ris,
               SISadj_d2000 = sis_top(tt_adj, 2000), Random_d2000 = sample(p, 2000))
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sets), function(m) {
    sel <- sets[[m]]; Xs <- scale(G2[, sel]); Xs[is.na(Xs)] <- 0
    cc <- abs(crossprod(Xc, Xs)) / (n - 1)
    data.frame(scenario = scn_name, rep = b, method = m, exact = mean(causal %in% sel),
               locus = mean(apply(cc, 1, max) >= 0.7),
               anc_cor = mean(abs(crossprod(anc_axis, Xs)) / (n - 1)), size = length(sel))
  }))
}
sim_file <- file.path("cache", "sim_results.rds")
if (USE_CACHE && file.exists(sim_file)) {
  sim_res <- readRDS(sim_file)
} else {
  sim_res <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(sim_scenarios), function(sn) do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(SIM_B), function(b) {
    cat(sprintf("[simulation] %s replicate %d\n", sn, b)); sim_one(sn, b)}))))
  saveRDS(sim_res, sim_file)
}
```

```{r sim-plots, fig.height = 8}
sim_res$method <- factor(sim_res$method, levels = c("SIS_d120", "SIS_d2000", "RIS", "SISadj_d2000", "Random_d2000"))
par(mfrow = c(3, 3), mar = c(6, 4, 3, 1))
for (sn in names(sim_scenarios)) {
  d <- sim_res[sim_res$scenario == sn, ]
  boxplot(exact ~ method, data = d, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, ylim = c(0, 1), main = paste(sn, ": exact recovery"), xlab = "", ylab = "fraction of causal SNPs", col = "steelblue")
  boxplot(locus ~ method, data = d, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, ylim = c(0, 1), main = paste(sn, ": locus recovery"), xlab = "", ylab = "fraction tagged (|r| >= 0.7)", col = "darkorange")
  boxplot(anc_cor ~ method, data = d, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, main = paste(sn, ": ancestry tagging"), xlab = "", ylab = "mean |cor| with axis 1", col = "darkgreen")
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
sim_tab <- aggregate(cbind(exact, locus, anc_cor, size) ~ scenario + method, data = sim_res, FUN = mean)
knitr::kable(sim_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = sprintf("Semi-synthetic simulation, mean over %d replicates", SIM_B))
```

            g("A_sparse", "SIS_d2000", "exact"), g("A_sparse", "SIS_d2000", "locus")))

Locus recovery in B: SIS %.2f versus adjusted SIS %.2f.\n",

# 6. The dense baseline, and pitfalls of screen-then-fit pipelines

**GBLUP** (genomic best linear unbiased prediction) is the standard genomic-prediction baseline: ridge regression
on *all* SNPs, computed through the n x n relationship matrix $K$ as kernel ridge,
$\hat y_* = K_{*,tr}(K_{tr,tr}+\lambda I)^{-1}y_{tr}$. With no supervised screening, $\lambda$ can be tuned on the
training data by closed-form leave-one-out CV, $e_i/(1-h_{ii})$ (equivalently, by the closed-form NIG marginal
likelihood, "evidence"). We also fit a Gaussian-kernel version to check for nonlinearity.

```{r e0-run}
run_rep_e0 <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; ym <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - ym; y_new_c <- y_te - ym
  K_tt <- Kfull[tr, tr]; K_et <- Kfull[te, tr]
  lin <- kernel_all(K_tt, K_et, y_c, y_new_c, LAM_GRID)
  il <- which.min(lin$loo); ie <- which.max(lin$ev)
  d_tr <- diag(K_tt); d_te <- dK[te]
  D_tt <- outer(d_tr, d_tr, "+") - 2 * K_tt; D_et <- outer(d_te, d_tr, "+") - 2 * K_et
  th <- median(D_tt[upper.tri(D_tt)])
  loo_min <- ev_max <- t_loo <- t_ev <- numeric(length(C_GRID))
  for (j in seq_along(C_GRID)) {
    kk <- kernel_all(exp(-pmax(D_tt, 0) / (2 * C_GRID[j] * th)), exp(-pmax(D_et, 0) / (2 * C_GRID[j] * th)),
                     y_c, y_new_c, LAM_GRID)
    jl <- which.min(kk$loo); je <- which.max(kk$ev)
    loo_min[j] <- kk$loo[jl]; ev_max[j] <- kk$ev[je]; t_loo[j] <- kk$test[jl]; t_ev[j] <- kk$test[je]
  }
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, baseline = mean((y_te - ym)^2), Lin_loo = lin$test[il], Lin_evid = lin$test[ie],
             lam_lin_loo = LAM_GRID[il], lam_lin_evid = LAM_GRID[ie],
             RBF_loo = t_loo[which.min(loo_min)], c_loo = C_GRID[which.min(loo_min)],
             RBF_evid = t_ev[which.max(ev_max)], c_evid = C_GRID[which.max(ev_max)])
}
e0 <- run_seeds("e0", run_rep_e0)
```

```{r e0-plots, fig.height = 5}

rng <- range(c(si$RP_agg, e0$Lin_loo))
plot(e0$Lin_loo, si$RP_agg, pch = 19, xlim = rng, ylim = rng, xlab = "full-SNP GBLUP test MSPE", ylab = "aggregated TARP test MSPE",
     main = "Each point = one split"); abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
plot(e0$Lin_loo, e0$RBF_loo, pch = 19, xlab = "GBLUP (linear kernel)", ylab = "Gaussian kernel", main = "Linear vs Gaussian kernel, no screening")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)
barplot(table(factor(e0$c_loo, levels = C_GRID)), col = "steelblue", border = NA, xlab = "bandwidth multiplier chosen by LOOCV",
        ylab = "splits", main = "Nonlinearity preference (16 = linear limit)")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
dd <- si$RP_agg - e0$Lin_loo
cat(sprintf("GBLUP: mean MSPE %.1f (R2 %.3f). Aggregated TARP: %.1f. GBLUP better by %.1f (SE %.1f) in %d of %d splits. Gaussian minus linear kernel without screening: %.2f (SE %.2f).\n",
            mean(e0$Lin_loo), mean(1 - e0$Lin_loo / e0$baseline), mean(si$RP_agg), mean(dd), sem(dd), sum(dd > 0), nrow(e0),
            mean(e0$RBF_loo - e0$Lin_loo), sem(e0$RBF_loo - e0$Lin_loo)))
```

## 6.1 Pitfall 1: leakage of test labels into screening

Screening uses the response, so it must see **training rows only**. Using all rows (a one-argument slip) lets the test
labels choose the predictors. The block below repeats RIS-PCR with that slip.

```{r leak-run}
run_rep_leak <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - y_mean
  tt <- screen_scores(seq_len(n), y_all)                        # LEAK: all rows, test labels included
  r <- sign(tt) * sqrt(tt^2 / (tt^2 + n - 2)); q_in <- abs(r)^max(0, (1 + log(p / n)) / 2); q_in <- q_in / max(q_in)
  inc <- which(rbinom(p, 1, q_in) == 1)
  X <- std_cols(G2[, inc], tr, te)
  V <- prcomp(X$tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM)$rotation[, 1:K_DIM]
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, PCA_leaky = nig_mspe(X$tr %*% V, X$other %*% V, y_c, y_mean, y_te), n_screened = length(inc))
}
leak <- run_seeds("leak", run_rep_leak)
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(list("screening on training rows\n(correct)" = si$PCA, "screening on all rows\n(leaky)" = leak$PCA_leaky),
        ylab = "test MSPE of RIS-PCR", col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"), main = "Leakage flatters the screened model")
barplot(c(correct = mean(1 - si$PCA / si$baseline), leaky = mean(1 - leak$PCA_leaky / si$baseline)), col = c("steelblue", "firebrick"),
        border = NA, ylab = "test R-squared", main = "Apparent versus honest R-squared")
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
cat(sprintf("RIS-PCR test MSPE %.1f with correct screening versus %.1f when the test labels leak into screening (%.0f%% lower, R-squared %.3f versus %.3f).\n",
            mean(si$PCA), mean(leak$PCA_leaky), 100 * (1 - mean(leak$PCA_leaky) / mean(si$PCA)),
            mean(1 - si$PCA / si$baseline), mean(1 - leak$PCA_leaky / si$baseline)))
```

## 6.2 Pitfall 2: tuning on the same data that screening has already used

If the SNPs were chosen because they correlate with the *training* response, any criterion computed afterwards on
the same samples (leave-one-out CV, evidence, an inner CV that does not repeat the screening) is over-confident
about the screened SNPs and picks too little regularization. The correct protocol is **nested**: inside each inner
fold, repeat the whole pipeline (screen, standardize, fit) on that fold's training rows and score on its held-out
rows. The comparison below uses the same screened SNPs and the same final model (ridge on a linear kernel) with
three tuning rules, plus the unscreened GBLUP where the in-sample rules are valid.

```{r e1-helpers}
pca_ridge <- function(Z_tr, Z_te, y_c, y_mean, y_te, lam_grid) {   # ridge on orthogonal PCA scores, evidence-tuned
  n_ <- length(y_c); d <- colSums(Z_tr^2); zy <- as.numeric(crossprod(Z_tr, y_c))
  ytil2 <- zy^2 / d; rest <- max(sum(y_c^2) - sum(ytil2), 0)
  ev <- vapply(lam_grid, function(l) log_evidence(d / l, ytil2, rest, n_), numeric(1)); i <- which.max(ev)
  pred_at <- function(l) as.numeric(Z_te %*% (zy / (d + l))) + y_mean
  list(mspe_fixed = mean((y_te - pred_at(1))^2), mspe_evid = mean((y_te - pred_at(lam_grid[i]))^2), lam = lam_grid[i])
}
kernel_set <- function(X_tr, X_o, c_grid) {                      # linear and Gaussian kernels from one Gram computation
  p_g <- ncol(X_tr); Gtr <- tcrossprod(X_tr); Go <- tcrossprod(X_o, X_tr)
  rn_tr <- diag(Gtr); rn_o <- rowSums(X_o^2)
  D_tr <- outer(rn_tr, rn_tr, "+") - 2 * Gtr; D_o <- outer(rn_o, rn_tr, "+") - 2 * Go
  th <- median(D_tr[upper.tri(D_tr)])
  list(lin = list(K = Gtr / p_g, Ko = Go / p_g),
       rbf = lapply(c_grid, function(cc) list(K = exp(-pmax(D_tr, 0) / (2 * cc * th)), Ko = exp(-pmax(D_o, 0) / (2 * cc * th)))))
}
curves_for <- function(ks, y_c, y_new_c, lam_grid) {
  list(lin = mse_curve(kernel_curve(ks$lin$K, ks$lin$Ko, y_c, lam_grid), y_new_c),
       rbf = t(vapply(ks$rbf, function(k) mse_curve(kernel_curve(k$K, k$Ko, y_c, lam_grid), y_new_c), numeric(length(lam_grid)))))
}
```

```{r e1-run}
# (a) in-sample tuning on the screened data: PCA ridge by evidence, linear-kernel ridge by evidence and by LOOCV
run_rep_e1 <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - y_mean
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); X <- std_cols(G2[, sc$inc], tr, te); X_tr <- X$tr; X_te <- X$other; p_g <- ncol(X_tr)
  V <- prcomp(X_tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM)$rotation[, 1:K_DIM]
  pr <- pca_ridge(X_tr %*% V, X_te %*% V, y_c, y_mean, y_te, LAM_GRID)
  lin <- kernel_all(tcrossprod(X_tr) / p_g, tcrossprod(X_te, X_tr) / p_g, y_c, y_te - y_mean, LAM_GRID)
  il <- which.min(lin$loo); ie <- which.max(lin$ev)
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, n_screened = p_g, PCA_fixed = pr$mspe_fixed, PCA_evid = pr$mspe_evid, lam_PCA = pr$lam,
             Lin_evid = lin$test[ie], Lin_loo = lin$test[il], lam_lin_evid = LAM_GRID[ie], lam_lin_loo = LAM_GRID[il])
}
e1 <- run_seeds("e1", run_rep_e1, legacy = "exp1_results.rds")

# (b) honest tuning: nested CV with the screening repeated inside every inner fold
run_rep_e1b <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr)
  sc0 <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); sc <- std_cols(G2[, sc0$inc], tr, te)
  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 7)
  fold <- sample(rep(seq_len(K_IN), length.out = length(tr)))
  cv_lin <- matrix(0, K_IN, length(LAM_GRID)); cv_rbf <- array(0, c(K_IN, length(C_GRID), length(LAM_GRID)))
  for (f in seq_len(K_IN)) {
    in_tr <- tr[fold != f]; in_va <- tr[fold == f]; y_in <- y_all[in_tr]; ym <- mean(y_in)
    sf0 <- screen_set(in_tr, y_in); sf <- std_cols(G2[, sf0$inc], in_tr, in_va)         # re-screen INSIDE the fold
    cv <- curves_for(kernel_set(sf$tr, sf$other, C_GRID), y_in - ym, y_all[in_va] - ym, LAM_GRID)
    cv_lin[f, ] <- cv$lin; cv_rbf[f, , ] <- cv$rbf
  }
  cvl <- colMeans(cv_lin); il <- which.min(cvl)
  cvr <- apply(cv_rbf, c(2, 3), mean); ib <- arrayInd(which.min(cvr), dim(cvr)); jc <- ib[1, 1]; jl <- ib[1, 2]
  te_cv <- curves_for(kernel_set(sc$tr, sc$other, C_GRID), y_tr - y_mean, y_te - y_mean, LAM_GRID)
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, n_screened = ncol(sc$tr), Lin_honest = te_cv$lin[il], RBF_honest = te_cv$rbf[jc, jl],
             Lin_oracle = min(te_cv$lin), RBF_oracle = min(te_cv$rbf),
             lam_lin = LAM_GRID[il], lam_rbf = LAM_GRID[jl], c_sel = C_GRID[jc], cv_lin_min = min(cvl), cv_rbf_min = min(cvr))
}
e1b <- run_seeds("e1b", run_rep_e1b, legacy = "exp1b_results.rds")
```

```{r e1-plots, fig.height = 5}

                 "screened data\nnested CV" = log10(e1b$lam_lin), "all SNPs\nLOOCV" = log10(e0$lam_lin_loo),
                 "all SNPs\nevidence" = log10(e0$lam_lin_evid))
boxplot(lam_list, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.75, ylab = "log10(lambda) chosen", col = c(rep("firebrick", 2), "steelblue", rep("grey70", 2)),
        main = "Regularization chosen by each tuning rule")
abline(h = log10(LAM_GRID[1]), lty = 3)
mse_list <- list("screened\nLOOCV" = e1$Lin_loo, "screened\nevidence" = e1$Lin_evid, "screened\nnested CV" = e1b$Lin_honest,
                 "all SNPs\nLOOCV (GBLUP)" = e0$Lin_loo, "TARP\naggregated" = si$RP_agg)
boxplot(mse_list, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.75, ylab = "test MSPE", col = c(rep("firebrick", 2), "steelblue", "grey70", "darkgreen"),
        main = "Test error by tuning rule (same screened SNPs)")

pit <- data.frame(Procedure = c("TARP, one projection", "TARP, aggregated (paper)", "Screened ridge, LOOCV on screened data",
                                "Screened ridge, evidence on screened data", "Screened ridge, nested CV (re-screening)",
                                "Full-SNP ridge, LOOCV (no screening)", "Full-SNP ridge, evidence (no screening)"),
                  Mean_MSPE = c(mean(si$RP_single), mean(si$RP_agg), mean(e1$Lin_loo), mean(e1$Lin_evid), mean(e1b$Lin_honest),
                                mean(e0$Lin_loo), mean(e0$Lin_evid)),
                  Median_log10_lambda = c(NA, NA, median(log10(e1$lam_lin_loo)), median(log10(e1$lam_lin_evid)),
                                          median(log10(e1b$lam_lin)), median(log10(e0$lam_lin_loo)), median(log10(e0$lam_lin_evid))))
knitr::kable(pit, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Pitfalls in one table (FT10 test MSPE)")
```

The in-sample criteria choose a far smaller $\lambda$ than nested CV (LOOCV runs into the bottom of the grid) and give
the worst test error; nested CV fixes it. With no screening, LOOCV and evidence agree and give the same error: this
is a natural experiment confirming that the screening step, not the criterion, causes the bias. The paper's own
design (a $\delta$ formula, an $m_n$ range, averaging) avoids data-driven tuning after screening altogether.

# 7. Does screening add anything to a dense kernel? Targeted GBLUP

Screening is good at finding large-effect SNPs, which a dense ridge dilutes. **Targeted GBLUP** keeps the dense kernel
and adds TARP's own screened set as a second kernel, $K = K_{full} + w\,K_{screened}$: screened SNPs receive a
prior-variance boost of about $1 + w\,p/p_{screened}$. $w=0$ is GBLUP; large $w$ approaches the screened-only ridge.
$(w,\lambda)$ are chosen by nested CV with re-screening inside each fold.

```{r e3-run}
run_rep_e3 <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr)
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); Ks_all <- screened_gram(sc$inc)
  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 7)
  fold <- sample(rep(seq_len(K_IN), length.out = length(tr)))
  cv <- array(0, c(K_IN, length(W_GRID), length(LAM_GRID)))
  for (f in seq_len(K_IN)) {
    in_tr <- tr[fold != f]; in_va <- tr[fold == f]; y_in <- y_all[in_tr]; ym <- mean(y_in)
    Ks_f <- screened_gram(screen_set(in_tr, y_in)$inc)                           # re-screen inside the fold
    for (iw in seq_along(W_GRID)) {
      w <- W_GRID[iw]
      cv[f, iw, ] <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Kfull[in_tr, in_tr] + w * Ks_f[in_tr, in_tr],
                                             Kfull[in_va, in_tr] + w * Ks_f[in_va, in_tr], y_in - ym, LAM_GRID),
                               y_all[in_va] - ym)
    }
  }
  cvm <- apply(cv, c(2, 3), mean); jl_w <- apply(cvm, 1, which.min)
  best <- arrayInd(which.min(cvm), dim(cvm)); iw_star <- best[1, 1]; il_star <- best[1, 2]
  te_m <- t(vapply(seq_along(W_GRID), function(iw) {
    w <- W_GRID[iw]
    mse_curve(kernel_curve(Kfull[tr, tr] + w * Ks_all[tr, tr], Kfull[te, tr] + w * Ks_all[te, tr], y_tr - y_mean, LAM_GRID),
              y_te - y_mean)
  }, numeric(length(LAM_GRID))))
  out <- data.frame(seed = seed_i, n_screened = length(sc$inc), TwoK_honest = te_m[iw_star, il_star],
                    GBLUP_nested = te_m[1, jl_w[1]], TwoK_oracle = min(te_m), w_sel = W_GRID[iw_star],
                    lam_sel = LAM_GRID[il_star], cv_min = min(cvm))
  for (iw in seq_along(W_GRID)) out[[paste0("T_w", W_GRID[iw])]] <- te_m[iw, jl_w[iw]]
  out
}
e3 <- run_seeds("e3", run_rep_e3, legacy = "exp3_results.rds")
```

# 8. Structure-aware group screening

The project's central structural idea is to screen **groups** of correlated SNPs instead of single SNPs (the GSIS
statistic of Agarwal, Dutta and Mukhopadhyay for grouped covariates): score a group by the joint explanatory power
of all its members, $\|P(X_{(k)})y\|^2/p_k$, then keep groups with probability proportional to a power of that score.
Groups should reflect LD. As a practical proxy for LD blocks, SNPs among the 50,000 strongest marginal candidates are
**clustered by their loadings in a PCA/correspondence-analysis embedding** (for strictly binary genotypes this
embedding is the same as the standardized-PCA one), giving about 500 groups of about 100 SNPs. Only the GSIS
*screening statistic* is implemented here, not the full reversible-jump search of the grouped-covariate paper.
Two details matter: the group exponent $\delta_g=\max\{0,(1+\log(n_g/n))/2\}$ collapses to zero, i.e. no screening at
all, if too few groups are formed (an earlier version of this analysis clustered only the 8,718 RIS survivors into 87
groups and silently reproduced RIS-PCR exactly), and the group set must be capped in size to fit in memory.

```{r group-run}
run_rep_group <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; y_mean <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - y_mean
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); r <- sc$r
  X <- std_cols(G2[, sc$inc], tr, te); X_tr <- X$tr; X_te <- X$other; p_g <- ncol(X_tr)
  Om <- tarp_omega(p_g, K_DIM); RIS_random <- nig_mspe(X_tr %*% Om, X_te %*% Om, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
  V <- prcomp(X_tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM)$rotation[, 1:K_DIM]
  RIS_PCA <- nig_mspe(X_tr %*% V, X_te %*% V, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
  K_CAND <- 50000
  cand <- order(abs(r), decreasing = TRUE)[1:K_CAND]
  Xc <- std_cols(G2[, cand], tr, te)
  emb <- prcomp(Xc$tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = 30)$rotation[, 1:30]
  km <- kmeans(emb, centers = round(K_CAND / 100), iter.max = 50, nstart = 5)
  group_list <- split(seq_len(K_CAND), km$cluster); n_groups <- length(group_list)
  gsis_one <- function(cols_local) {
    cols <- cand[cols_local]
    Xk <- scale(G2[tr, cols, drop = FALSE], center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)
    beta <- tryCatch(solve(crossprod(Xk) + diag(1, ncol(Xk)), crossprod(Xk, y_c)), error = function(e) rep(0, ncol(Xk)))
    sum((Xk %*% beta)^2) / length(cols)
  }
  gq <- unlist(mclapply(group_list, gsis_one, mc.cores = N_CORES))
  delta_g <- max(0, (1 + log(n_groups / length(tr))) / 2); q_g <- (gq / max(gq))^delta_g
  inc_g <- cand[unlist(group_list[rbinom(n_groups, 1, q_g) == 1])]
  max_cols <- floor(1.5e9 / (n * 8))                                            # memory guard
  if (length(inc_g) > max_cols) {
    sc_snp <- numeric(p); for (k in which(q_g > 0)) sc_snp[cand[group_list[[k]]]] <- gq[k]
    inc_g <- inc_g[order(sc_snp[inc_g], decreasing = TRUE)[seq_len(max_cols)]]
  }
  Xg <- std_cols(G2[, inc_g], tr, te)
  Og <- tarp_omega(ncol(Xg$tr), K_DIM); GSIS_random <- nig_mspe(Xg$tr %*% Og, Xg$other %*% Og, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
  Vg <- prcomp(Xg$tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = K_DIM)$rotation[, 1:K_DIM]
  GSIS_PCA <- nig_mspe(Xg$tr %*% Vg, Xg$other %*% Vg, y_c, y_mean, y_te)
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, baseline = mean((y_te - y_mean)^2), RIS_random = RIS_random, RIS_PCA = RIS_PCA,
             GSIS_random = GSIS_random, GSIS_PCA = GSIS_PCA, n_groups = n_groups, delta_g = delta_g)
}
grp_res <- run_seeds("group", run_rep_group, legacy = "replication_results.rds")
```

```{r group-plots, fig.height = 5}
cells <- c("RIS_random", "RIS_PCA", "GSIS_random", "GSIS_PCA")
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
boxplot(grp_res[, cells], names = c("RIS\nrandom proj.", "RIS\nPCA", "group screen\nrandom proj.", "group screen\nPCA"),
        col = c("grey70", "steelblue", "grey70", "steelblue"), ylab = "test MSPE", main = "Individual versus group screening")
dgp <- list("group - individual\n(random proj.)" = grp_res$GSIS_random - grp_res$RIS_random,
            "group - individual\n(PCA)" = grp_res$GSIS_PCA - grp_res$RIS_PCA,
            "PCA - random proj.\n(individual)" = grp_res$RIS_PCA - grp_res$RIS_random)
boxplot(dgp, ylab = "MSPE difference", col = "darkorange", main = "Paired differences"); abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
knitr::kable(data.frame(Contrast = names(dgp), Mean = sapply(dgp, mean), SE = sapply(dgp, sem), Negative_in = sapply(dgp, function(x) sum(x < 0))),
             digits = 2, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Group-level screening and projection choice (random projection here is a single, unaggregated draw)")
cat(sprintf("Groups formed per split: %.0f (delta_g = %.2f, non-degenerate). Group screening with random projection: %.1f versus individual screening %.1f; with PCA: %.1f versus %.1f.\n",
            mean(grp_res$n_groups), mean(grp_res$delta_g), mean(grp_res$GSIS_random), mean(grp_res$RIS_random),
            mean(grp_res$GSIS_PCA), mean(grp_res$RIS_PCA)))
```

Group screening does not reliably beat individual screening: with a single random projection the two are
indistinguishable (the group version is noisier), and with PCA projection the individual rule is at least as good.
The one large, stable effect is the choice of projection (PCA against a single random draw), which the paper's
aggregation step removes (Section 4).


# 9. What is being predicted? Population structure, relatedness and within-lineage signal

Flowering time varies along the main ancestry gradient (Section 3.1), so part of any genome-wide predictor is
"which lineage is this accession from". Three analyses separate this from genuine within-lineage signal.

## 9.1 Latent class analysis (LCA) of the genotypes, fitted by EM

A latent class model for binary genotypes (a Bernoulli mixture) is fitted by the EM algorithm on a thinned, evenly
spaced panel of 800 SNPs with minor allele frequency at least 0.1: each accession gets soft class memberships
$R$ ($n\times K$), with class-specific allele probabilities $\theta_{kj}$ and mixing weights $\pi_k$. No response is used.
Neighbouring SNPs are not independent given the class, so BIC favors many classes; the classes are flexible ancestry
features, not a taxonomy.

```{r lca}
lca_em <- function(B, K, n_init = 10, iters = 300, tol = 1e-7) {
  n_ <- nrow(B); best <- NULL
  for (s in seq_len(n_init)) {
    R <- matrix(runif(n_ * K), n_, K); R <- R / rowSums(R); ll_old <- -Inf
    for (it in seq_len(iters)) {
      pi_k <- pmax(colMeans(R), 1e-8)                                              # M-step
      theta <- sweep(t(R) %*% B + 0.5, 1, colSums(R) + 1, "/")
      logp <- B %*% t(log(theta)) + (1 - B) %*% t(log(1 - theta))                  # E-step
      logp <- sweep(logp, 2, log(pi_k), "+")
      m <- apply(logp, 1, max); lse <- m + log(rowSums(exp(logp - m)))
      R <- exp(logp - lse); ll <- sum(lse)
      if (abs(ll - ll_old) < tol * abs(ll)) break
      ll_old <- ll
    }
    if (is.null(best) || ll > best$ll) best <- list(R = R, ll = ll)
  }
  best
}
set.seed(2025)
Xp <- G2[, round(seq(1, p, length.out = 30000))]; f_l <- colMeans(Xp) / 2
Xp <- Xp[, f_l > 0.1 & f_l < 0.9]
B_lca <- (Xp[, round(seq(1, ncol(Xp), length.out = min(800, ncol(Xp))))] >= 1) * 1; rm(Xp)
K_LCA_SET <- c(2:8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 24)
lca_file <- file.path("cache", "lca_fits.rds")
if (USE_CACHE && file.exists(lca_file)) {
  fits <- readRDS(lca_file)
} else {
  fits <- lapply(K_LCA_SET, function(k) lca_em(B_lca, k)); names(fits) <- K_LCA_SET; saveRDS(fits, lca_file)
}
bic <- sapply(names(fits), function(k) { k <- as.integer(k); -2 * fits[[as.character(k)]]$ll + ((k - 1) + k * ncol(B_lca)) * log(n) })
Rmem8 <- fits[["8"]]$R; hard8 <- max.col(Rmem8)
cat("Class sizes at K = 8:", paste(table(hard8), collapse = " / "), "\nMean FT10 by class:", paste(round(tapply(y_all, hard8, mean), 1), collapse = " / "), "\n")
```

plot(as.integer(names(bic)), bic, type = "b", pch = 19, xlab = "latent classes K", ylab = "BIC", main = "LCA: BIC by K")

## 9.2 Relatedness-only predictors, ancestry-explicit GBLUP and within-lineage correlation

Predictors that use **only relatedness** (no SNP effects): the mean FT10 of the k genetically closest training
accessions (kNN on the genomic distance), a Nadaraya-Watson kernel smoother on the same distances, and LCA class
memberships. They are compared with GBLUP, and with ancestry-explicit GBLUP ("Q+K": the dense kernel plus a linear
kernel on the LCA memberships or the top-5 axes, weight chosen by LOOCV). Finally, the **within-class correlation**:
test accessions and their predictions are centered within their latent class, and the pooled correlation is computed.
A predictor that only knows lineage scores about zero.

```{r struct-run}
K_NN_GRID <- c(1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 20, 30, 50, 80); H_GRID <- c(0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1)
WQ_GRID <- c(0, 0.1, 0.3, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100); K_WITHIN <- c(4, 6, 8, 12)
knn_predict <- function(D_tt, D_te, y_tr, k_grid) {
  n_tr <- length(y_tr); kmax <- max(k_grid); Dt <- D_tt; diag(Dt) <- Inf
  loo <- matrix(0, n_tr, length(k_grid))
  for (i in seq_len(n_tr)) { nn <- order(Dt[i, ])[1:kmax]; loo[i, ] <- (cumsum(y_tr[nn]) / seq_len(kmax))[k_grid] }
  kbest <- k_grid[which.min(colMeans((y_tr - loo)^2))]
  list(pred = vapply(seq_len(nrow(D_te)), function(i) mean(y_tr[order(D_te[i, ])[1:kbest]]), numeric(1)), k = kbest)
}
nw_apply <- function(D, y_tr, h, th, drop_self = FALSE) {
  W <- exp(-pmax(D, 0) / (2 * h * th)); if (drop_self) diag(W) <- 0
  den <- rowSums(W); num <- as.numeric(W %*% y_tr); ifelse(den < 1e-8, mean(y_tr), num / pmax(den, 1e-300))
}
nw_predict <- function(D_tt, D_te, y_tr, h_grid) {
  th <- median(D_tt[upper.tri(D_tt)])
  mse <- sapply(h_grid, function(h) mean((y_tr - nw_apply(D_tt, y_tr, h, th, TRUE))^2)); hb <- h_grid[which.min(mse)]
  list(pred = nw_apply(D_te, y_tr, hb, th), h = hb)
}
within_cor <- function(y, pr, g, min_n = 5) {
  tb <- table(g); keep <- as.integer(names(tb)[tb >= min_n]); ix <- g %in% keep
  yc <- y[ix] - ave(y[ix], g[ix]); pc <- pr[ix] - ave(pr[ix], g[ix])
  c(r = cor(yc, pc), slope = sum(yc * pc) / sum(pc^2), n = sum(ix), frac = sum(yc^2) / sum((y - mean(y))^2))
}
lin_kernel <- function(M) { Kq <- tcrossprod(scale(M, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)); Kq / mean(diag(Kq)) }
qk_fit <- function(Kq, tr, te, y_c, y_new_c) {
  res <- lapply(WQ_GRID, function(w) kernel_all(Kfull[tr, tr] + w * Kq[tr, tr], Kfull[te, tr] + w * Kq[te, tr], y_c, y_new_c, LAM_GRID))
  loo <- sapply(res, function(r) r$loo); ib <- arrayInd(which.min(loo), dim(loo))
  list(mspe = res[[ib[1, 2]]]$test[ib[1, 1]], w = WQ_GRID[ib[1, 2]])
}
K_lca_kernel <- lin_kernel(Rmem8[, -ncol(Rmem8), drop = FALSE]); K_pc_kernel <- lin_kernel(pcs5)
hard_k <- lapply(K_WITHIN, function(k) max.col(fits[[as.character(k)]]$R)); names(hard_k) <- K_WITHIN

run_rep_struct <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_all[tr]; y_te <- y_all[te]; ym <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - ym; y_new_c <- y_te - ym
  X1 <- cbind(1, Rmem8[, -ncol(Rmem8), drop = FALSE])                       # class-membership-only predictor
  beta <- solve(crossprod(X1[tr, ]) + 1e-6 * diag(ncol(X1)), crossprod(X1[tr, ], y_tr))
  qk_l <- qk_fit(K_lca_kernel, tr, te, y_c, y_new_c); qk_p <- qk_fit(K_pc_kernel, tr, te, y_c, y_new_c)
  D_tt <- gdist(tr, tr); D_te <- gdist(te, tr)
  kn <- knn_predict(D_tt, D_te, y_tr, K_NN_GRID); nw <- nw_predict(D_tt, D_te, y_tr, H_GRID); gb <- gblup_fit(tr, te, y_tr)
  out <- data.frame(seed = seed_i, baseline = mean((y_te - ym)^2), class_only = mean((y_te - X1[te, ] %*% beta)^2),
                    GBLUP = mean((y_te - gb$pred)^2), QK_LCA = qk_l$mspe, w_LCA = qk_l$w, QK_PC = qk_p$mspe, w_PC = qk_p$w,
                    kNN = mean((y_te - kn$pred)^2), k_sel = kn$k, NW = mean((y_te - nw$pred)^2), h_sel = nw$h)
  for (k in K_WITHIN) {
    g_te <- hard_k[[as.character(k)]][te]; wg <- within_cor(y_te, gb$pred, g_te); wk <- within_cor(y_te, kn$pred, g_te)
    out[[paste0("wcG_", k)]] <- unname(wg["r"]); out[[paste0("wcK_", k)]] <- unname(wk["r"]); out[[paste0("wfrac_", k)]] <- unname(wg["frac"])
  }
  out
}
struct <- run_seeds("struct", run_rep_struct)
```

  mean(sapply(seq_len(N_REPS), function(s) {
    sp <- make_split(s); X <- cbind(1, Rk[, -ncol(Rk), drop = FALSE])

    mean((y_all[sp$te] - X[sp$te, ] %*% b)^2)
  }))
}

            mean(dq[[1]]), mean(dq[[2]])))
```

Relatedness and ancestry explain a large share of the predictable signal, but GBLUP predicts *within* lineages too, so
comparisons between SNP-level methods are comparisons on genuine genome-wide signal. Part of that within-lineage
signal is fine-scale relatedness (the nearest-relatives predictor also has within-class skill); since GBLUP is itself a
kernel smoother, fine-scale relatedness and additive SNP effects cannot be separated further with these data.
Two further structure-based ideas (a fixed-gating mixture of experts and a shared-plus-class-interaction kernel) were
tried during development and gave no gain (the mixture of experts was clearly worse and unstable); they are not
reproduced here.

# 10. Calibration of prediction intervals

TARP's NIG posterior yields a Student-t predictive distribution, $y_*\sim t_{n+2a}\!\big(z_*'\mu,\; s^2(1+z_*'Wz_*)\big)$.
Its coverage on new accessions is checked against **split-conformal** alternatives around GBLUP, which carry a
distribution-free finite-sample guarantee. A–D are fitted on 75% of the training rows (the rest calibrate); E–F use
all training rows and no calibration set. All target 90% coverage.

| Key | Interval |
|---|---|
| A | GBLUP + split conformal, absolute residuals |
| B | GBLUP as a kernel-NIG model: Student-t predictive interval |
| C | GBLUP + conformal on residuals normalized by the GP predictive sd |
| D | like A, calibrated separately within each of three ancestry clusters (Mondrian) |
| E | TARP-style: screening + PCA + NIG interval |
| F | TARP-style: screening + one random projection + NIG interval |

```{r e2-helpers}
conf_q <- function(scores, alpha) { m <- length(scores); k <- ceiling((m + 1) * (1 - alpha)); if (k > m) Inf else sort(scores)[k] }
interval_metrics <- function(lo, hi, y, g, alpha) {
  hit <- (y >= lo) & (y <= hi)
  isc <- (hi - lo) + (2 / alpha) * pmax(lo - y, 0) + (2 / alpha) * pmax(y - hi, 0)            # Winkler interval score
  gcov <- sapply(seq_len(K_GROUPS), function(k) if (any(g == k)) mean(hit[g == k]) else NA_real_)
  list(cov = mean(hit), wid = mean(hi - lo), iscore = mean(isc), gcov = gcov, mincov = min(gcov, na.rm = TRUE))
}
gp_fit <- function(K_tt, y_c, lam_grid, a = 0.01, b = 0.01) {
  n_ <- length(y_c); eg <- eigen(K_tt, symmetric = TRUE); e <- pmax(eg$values, 0); U <- eg$vectors
  yt <- as.numeric(crossprod(U, y_c)); S <- outer(e, lam_grid, function(ei, li) ei / (ei + li))
  loo <- colMeans(((y_c - U %*% (S * yt)) / pmax(1 - (U^2) %*% S, 1e-8))^2); lam <- lam_grid[which.min(loo)]
  list(e = e, U = U, yt = yt, lam = lam, s2 = (2 * b + sum(yt^2 / (1 + e / lam))) / (n_ + 2 * a), df = n_ + 2 * a)
}
gp_predict <- function(fit, K_new, k_diag) {
  KU <- K_new %*% fit$U
  list(mean_c = as.numeric(KU %*% (fit$yt / (fit$e + fit$lam))),
       v = pmax(k_diag - rowSums(sweep(KU^2, 2, fit$e + fit$lam, "/")), 0))
}
nig_interval <- function(Z_tr, Z_te, yc, ym, alpha, a = 0.01, b = 0.01) {         # the paper's predictive distribution
  n_ <- length(yc); m <- ncol(Z_tr); A <- diag(m) + crossprod(Z_tr); mu <- solve(A, crossprod(Z_tr, yc))
  s2 <- (sum(yc^2) - as.numeric(crossprod(mu, A %*% mu)) + 2 * b) / (n_ + 2 * a)
  vfac <- 1 + colSums(t(Z_te) * solve(A, t(Z_te)))
  half <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, n_ + 2 * a) * sqrt(s2 * vfac); mid <- as.numeric(Z_te %*% mu) + ym
  list(lo = mid - half, hi = mid + half)
}
```

```{r e2-run}
run_rep_e2 <- function(seed_i) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_te <- y_all[te]; g_te <- grp[te]; y_tr <- y_all[tr]; ym <- mean(y_tr); yc <- y_tr - ym
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); X <- std_cols(G2[, sc$inc], tr, te); X_tr <- X$tr; X_te <- X$other
  pca <- prcomp(X_tr, center = FALSE, scale. = FALSE, rank. = 100)
  iv_E <- nig_interval(X_tr %*% pca$rotation, X_te %*% pca$rotation, yc, ym, ALPHA)
  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 13); Om <- tarp_omega(ncol(X_tr), 100)
  iv_F <- nig_interval(X_tr %*% Om, X_te %*% Om, yc, ym, ALPHA)
  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 11)
  cal_pos <- sample(seq_along(tr), size = round(0.25 * length(tr))); cal <- tr[cal_pos]; pt <- tr[-cal_pos]
  y_pt <- y_all[pt]; ym_pt <- mean(y_pt); y_cal <- y_all[cal]
  fit <- gp_fit(Kfull[pt, pt], y_pt - ym_pt, LAM_GRID)
  pc <- gp_predict(fit, Kfull[cal, pt, drop = FALSE], dK[cal]); pe <- gp_predict(fit, Kfull[te, pt, drop = FALSE], dK[te])
  mu_cal <- pc$mean_c + ym_pt; mu_te <- pe$mean_c + ym_pt; res_cal <- abs(y_cal - mu_cal)
  sdf_cal <- sqrt(1 + pc$v / fit$lam); sdf_te <- sqrt(1 + pe$v / fit$lam)
  qA <- conf_q(res_cal, ALPHA); half_B <- qt(1 - ALPHA / 2, fit$df) * sqrt(fit$s2) * sdf_te
  qC <- conf_q(res_cal / sdf_cal, ALPHA); g_cal <- grp[cal]
  qD <- sapply(seq_len(K_GROUPS), function(k) { s <- res_cal[g_cal == k]; if (length(s) >= MIN_G) conf_q(s, ALPHA) else qA })
  ints <- list(A_conformal = list(lo = mu_te - qA, hi = mu_te + qA), B_bayes_t = list(lo = mu_te - half_B, hi = mu_te + half_B),
               C_gp_conformal = list(lo = mu_te - qC * sdf_te, hi = mu_te + qC * sdf_te),
               D_mondrian = list(lo = mu_te - qD[g_te], hi = mu_te + qD[g_te]), E_TARP_PCA_NIG = iv_E, F_TARP_RP_NIG = iv_F)
  out <- data.frame(seed = seed_i, mspe_GBLUP75 = mean((y_te - mu_te)^2))
  for (nm in names(ints)) {
    mm <- interval_metrics(ints[[nm]]$lo, ints[[nm]]$hi, y_te, g_te, ALPHA)
    out[[paste0("cov_", nm)]] <- mm$cov; out[[paste0("wid_", nm)]] <- mm$wid; out[[paste0("isc_", nm)]] <- mm$iscore
    out[[paste0("mincov_", nm)]] <- mm$mincov
    for (k in seq_len(K_GROUPS)) out[[paste0("gcov_", nm, "_g", k)]] <- mm$gcov[k]
  }
  out
}
e2 <- run_seeds("e2", run_rep_e2, legacy = "exp2_results.rds")
```

```{r e2-plots, fig.height = 6}
nms <- c("A_conformal", "B_bayes_t", "C_gp_conformal", "D_mondrian", "E_TARP_PCA_NIG", "F_TARP_RP_NIG")
lab <- c("A conformal", "B Bayes t", "C GP-normalized\nconformal", "D Mondrian", "E TARP PCA\nNIG", "F TARP RP\nNIG")
isG <- c(rep("steelblue", 4), rep("firebrick", 2))
cm <- sapply(nms, function(m) e2[[paste0("cov_", m)]]); mm <- sapply(nms, function(m) e2[[paste0("mincov_", m)]])
par(mfrow = c(2, 2), mar = c(7, 4, 3, 1))
boxplot(cm, names = lab, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, col = isG, ylab = "test coverage", main = "Coverage of nominal 90% intervals"); abline(h = 0.9, lty = 2)
boxplot(mm, names = lab, las = 2, cex.axis = 0.7, col = isG, ylab = "coverage in the worst ancestry cluster", main = "Worst-cluster coverage"); abline(h = 0.9, lty = 2)

plot(wd, cv, pch = 19, col = isG, cex = 1.5, xlab = "mean interval width (days)", ylab = "mean coverage", main = "Coverage against width")
text(wd, cv, c("A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"), pos = 3); abline(h = 0.9, lty = 2)
gt <- sapply(seq_len(K_GROUPS), function(k) sapply(nms, function(m) mean(e2[[paste0("gcov_", m, "_g", k)]], na.rm = TRUE)))
matplot(t(gt), type = "b", pch = 1:6, lty = 1, col = c(rep("steelblue", 4), rep("firebrick", 2)), xaxt = "n", ylab = "coverage",
        main = "Coverage within each ancestry cluster"); axis(1, at = seq_len(K_GROUPS), labels = paste("cluster", seq_len(K_GROUPS))); abline(h = 0.9, lty = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1), mar = c(5, 4, 4, 2))
cal_tab <- data.frame(Interval = gsub("\n", " ", lab), Coverage = colMeans(cm), Seed_SD = apply(cm, 2, sd),
                      Mean_width = wd, Interval_score = sapply(nms, function(m) mean(e2[[paste0("isc_", m)]])),
                      Worst_cluster_coverage = colMeans(mm))
knitr::kable(cal_tab, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE, caption = "Test-set coverage, width and interval score (lower is better)")
colnames(gt) <- paste0("cluster ", seq_len(K_GROUPS), " (", as.integer(table(grp)), " accessions)"); rownames(gt) <- gsub("\n", " ", lab)
knitr::kable(gt, digits = 3, caption = "Mean coverage within each ancestry cluster")
```

Intervals that rely on screened SNPs under-cover: screening has already used the training response, so the residual
variance is under-estimated. Intervals around the dense GBLUP model, with a calibration set that no screening step has
touched, reach the nominal level; the Bayesian t-interval from the kernel model is already close to calibrated. The
paper's statement that random-projection intervals cover better than PCA ones points the same way here
(F above E) but the difference is within noise. Each split has only 201 test accessions, so coverage per split is
uncertain by about 0.02.

# 11. A second trait (FT16), and a place for a third

```{r trait-fn}
run_rep_trait <- function(seed_i, y_full, pool, run_tarp = TRUE) {
  sp <- make_split(seed_i, pool); tr <- sp$tr; te <- sp$te
  y_tr <- y_full[tr]; y_te <- y_full[te]; ym <- mean(y_tr); y_c <- y_tr - ym; y_new_c <- y_te - ym
  base <- mean((y_te - ym)^2)
  sc <- screen_set(tr, y_tr); Ks_all <- screened_gram(sc$inc)
  g <- kernel_all(Kfull[tr, tr], Kfull[te, tr], y_c, y_new_c, LAM_GRID); GBLUP <- g$test[which.min(g$loo)]
  set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 7)
  fold <- sample(rep(seq_len(K_IN), length.out = length(tr)))
  cvw <- array(0, c(K_IN, length(W_GRID), length(LAM_GRID))); cvs <- matrix(0, K_IN, length(LAM_GRID))
  for (f in seq_len(K_IN)) {
    in_tr <- tr[fold != f]; in_va <- tr[fold == f]; y_in <- y_full[in_tr]; ymf <- mean(y_in); yv <- y_full[in_va] - ymf
    Ks_f <- screened_gram(screen_set(in_tr, y_in)$inc)
    for (iw in seq_along(W_GRID)) {
      wv <- W_GRID[iw]
      cvw[f, iw, ] <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Kfull[in_tr, in_tr] + wv * Ks_f[in_tr, in_tr], Kfull[in_va, in_tr] + wv * Ks_f[in_va, in_tr],
                                              y_in - ymf, LAM_GRID), yv)
    }
    cvs[f, ] <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Ks_f[in_tr, in_tr], Ks_f[in_va, in_tr], y_in - ymf, LAM_GRID), yv)
  }
  cvm <- apply(cvw, c(2, 3), mean); ib <- arrayInd(which.min(cvm), dim(cvm)); iw_s <- ib[1, 1]; il_s <- ib[1, 2]
  ils <- which.min(colMeans(cvs)); w_s <- W_GRID[iw_s]
  TGB <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Kfull[tr, tr] + w_s * Ks_all[tr, tr], Kfull[te, tr] + w_s * Ks_all[te, tr], y_c, LAM_GRID), y_new_c)[il_s]
  SCR <- mse_curve(kernel_curve(Ks_all[tr, tr], Ks_all[te, tr], y_c, LAM_GRID), y_new_c)[ils]
  AGG <- NA_real_
  if (run_tarp) {
    X <- std_cols(G2[, sc$inc], tr, te); set.seed(seed_i * 1000 + 17)
    AGG <- mean((y_te - agg_tarp_pred(X$tr, X$other, y_c, ym, p))^2)
  }
  data.frame(seed = seed_i, n_pool = length(pool), baseline = base, GBLUP = GBLUP, TGB = TGB, SCR = SCR, AGG = AGG, w_sel = w_s)
}
pool16 <- which(!is.na(y16)); cat("FT16: accessions with genotype and phenotype:", length(pool16), "\n")
t16 <- run_seeds("trait_FT16", function(s) run_rep_trait(s, y16, pool16), legacy = "trait_FT16_results.rds")
traits <- list(FT10 = NULL, FT16 = t16)
if (!is.null(THIRD_TRAIT$file)) {                        # optional third trait: set THIRD_TRAIT in the parameters chunk
  d3 <- read.csv(THIRD_TRAIT$file)
  y3 <- as.numeric(d3[[THIRD_TRAIT$y_col]][match(as.character(fam$sample.ID), as.character(d3[[THIRD_TRAIT$id_col]]))])
  pool3 <- which(!is.na(y3)); cat(THIRD_TRAIT$name, ": accessions with genotype and phenotype:", length(pool3), "\n")
  stopifnot(length(pool3) >= 200)
  traits[[THIRD_TRAIT$name]] <- run_seeds(paste0("trait_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]", "_", THIRD_TRAIT$name)),
                                          function(s) run_rep_trait(s, y3, pool3))
}
traits$FT10 <- data.frame(seed = e3$seed, baseline = si$baseline[match(e3$seed, si$seed)], GBLUP = e0$Lin_loo[match(e3$seed, e0$seed)],
                          TGB = e3$TwoK_honest, SCR = e1b$Lin_honest[match(e3$seed, e1b$seed)], AGG = si$RP_agg[match(e3$seed, si$seed)])
```

```{r trait-plots, fig.height = 5}
tr_rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(traits), function(nm) {
  df <- traits[[nm]]; ms <- c("GBLUP", "TGB", "SCR", "AGG")
  data.frame(Trait = nm, Method = ms, Mean_MSPE = sapply(ms, function(m) mean(df[[m]], na.rm = TRUE)),
             R2 = sapply(ms, function(m) mean(1 - df[[m]] / df$baseline, na.rm = TRUE)),
             Diff_vs_GBLUP = sapply(ms, function(m) mean(df[[m]] - df$GBLUP, na.rm = TRUE)),
             SE = sapply(ms, function(m) sem((df[[m]] - df$GBLUP)[!is.na(df[[m]])])),
             Beats_GBLUP = sapply(ms, function(m) sum(df[[m]] < df$GBLUP, na.rm = TRUE)),
             Pct_of_GBLUP_MSPE = sapply(ms, function(m) 100 * mean(df[[m]] - df$GBLUP, na.rm = TRUE) / mean(df$GBLUP)))
}))
rownames(tr_rows) <- NULL
knitr::kable(tr_rows, digits = 3, caption = "GBLUP = full SNP; TGB = targeted GBLUP; SCR = honest screened ridge; AGG = aggregated TARP. Last column: difference as % of GBLUP's MSPE")
par(mfrow = c(1, length(traits)))
for (nm in names(traits)) {
  df <- traits[[nm]]; d <- sapply(c("TGB", "SCR", "AGG"), function(m) 100 * (df[[m]] - df$GBLUP) / df$GBLUP)
  boxplot(d, col = "steelblue", ylab = "% difference in MSPE vs GBLUP", main = nm); abline(h = 0, lty = 2)
}
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

FT16 is the same accessions at another temperature and is strongly correlated with FT10, so agreement between the two
shows the result is not an artifact of the 10 degree measurement, not that it holds for traits with a different
genetic architecture. The key test of **when screening helps** is a trait dominated by a few large-effect loci
(for example a DOG1-related germination trait, available from the Dryad repository of Martinez-Berdeja et al. 2020 and
AraPheno): download it, convert to CSV, set `THIRD_TRAIT <- list(file = "...csv", id_col = "...", y_col = "...", name = "DOG1 germination")`
in the parameters chunk and re-render. The chunk above then runs the same four methods on it and adds it to the table.
If screening is going to beat a dense kernel anywhere, it should be there.
